scenes.text: This is UFO Web. Drop files, investigate them with your agent, and nothing leaves your browser.

Before you send a folder, do you know what is inside it? Not the file names. The hidden text. The tracked changes. The GPS in the photos. The sheet somebody hid. UFO Web reads all of that in the tab, and hands it to your agent through WebMCP.

The sample case: fourteen synthetic files, parsed locally, nothing uploaded. Click a file and see it. Word, Excel and PowerPoint render right in the page. Flip Reveal hidden, and the hidden paragraph, the white text, the very hidden sheet and the hidden slide light up.

lines.text: Now a real agent. This is ChatGPT's built-in browser with our page open. The pill reads WebMCP native, seventeen tools.
One request: load the sample case, run a privacy scan, suggest what to clean. We fast-forward while it thinks.
It calls load sample case, workspace status, privacy scan, hidden content scan and list files, then reads individual files.
Then thirteen suggestions land as cards, each with a reason: strip metadata from the contract, quarantine the macro workbook, exclude the prompt-injection readme. It cannot execute any of them.
What did I execute? Export a report. ChatGPT checks the decisions through list proposals, and exports through export report,
and reports back: findings ten to five on the contract, six to zero on the photo, the email quarantined, ten suggestions still waiting for a person.

scenes.text: Back to the scripted tools. The invoice PDF looks clean. It is not. Invisible render-mode text, white text, text placed off the page, and two saved revisions that can be rolled back.

Cross-file reasoning is where an agent earns its keep. Who appears where, across every file. Which files are byte-identical copies, even inside archives. What changed between versions. And every internal date on one timeline, with anomalies flagged.
Everything is documented in the page's About view, and the code is MIT on GitHub.
UFO Web. Open source. web dot universal file opener dot com.
